chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Lincoln Park and Johnson Park: brass band, dances, Easter and Mardi Gras
summary: As a boy in short pants Foster sneaked into the parks to hear brass bands and dance orchestras; Easter, New Year and the Mardi Gras season.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Before you were telling me. Well you see, I used to, but I was playing, I used to go back there, I remember, I remember once, they was playing at Johnson Park. I was Johnson Park. Oh. Right, see, Johnson Park was like, here, Lincoln Park was here. See? And, and Bab Frank Piller's band, Yeah. Bab Frank had a brass band, and had his orchestra too. Yeah. So they had this brass band playing, over at Lincoln Park, and Buddy Boehme, cut that, see, because, I'd slip in there, and short pants, and hide from the cops, because they'd chase you out, see, the cops would chase you. They'd say, get out of here boy, and then, and you'd go and hide somewhere, and then, still stay there, see. Cut the hole in there, and, and, and, and, all the children home. at the Lincoln Park. Yeah. Yeah, the, the band was stopped. The brass band? No, no, and they had, John had his, his orchestra too. Yeah. On a big stage, yeah. Playing from fourth, to seventh, seven, they'd knock off for lunch, then they'd go, in a big hall, they'd go to their halls, and play from eighth to fourth.

Well, let me tell you about that. You see, I used to go out, go out to that park, I was a kid, in short pants, and, uh, the brass band was played, John, and they had a trumpet player, who was Dutry, used to play in the brass band, alongside, with another trumpet player, from Al Jays, I've been trying to think of his name, real dark. Buddy Johnson. No, not Buddy, it wasn't Buddy. Harrison Bourne? Him, Harrison Bourne. He used to play, he used to play, in John's brass band, see, but John was playing bass drum, right? I thought he always played bass drum. Bass drum, but he only played bass drum, even there where they're sitting, where they're sitting down. Then, and at night, they'll go, and then he had this, this, uh, had, uh, Andrew Kimmel's, Andrew Kimmel's wife was playing piano. Margaret. Margaret, see, she played piano, see, now she played for the show. Now after the show, they didn't use no piano. They get on the stage, get on the stage, and play until four o'clock.

two fifty. Because Easter Sunday used to be our big day, was it? Oh yeah. Easter Sunday was our big day. New Year's Eve, man, everybody, New Year's Eve, Christmas, people went on to church. And, and, and after, 12 Tuesday, which was Mardi Gras day, see, everybody worked on Mardi Gras. Now after, now after, after Mardi Gras, they were every musician, musician, down in New Orleans, back in those days, and they wasn't called them, they was plasters, or cigar makers, see, or they go on part of the street, and the canned legs.
